story.title: PipePipe: NewPipe hard fork implementing SponsorBlock

draft:
A fork that finally gives YouTube viewers real control over sponsor segments.

I’ve been following NewPipe for years because it lets us stream YouTube without the Google‑tracking stack. PipePipe pushes the project a step further by embedding SponsorBlock directly into the client. No more manual extensions or separate apps—skip sponsorships with a single tap, all while staying in an open‑source, privacy‑first environment.

- The integration means the community‑maintained blocklist can be updated in real time, something NewPipe’s original architecture didn’t support natively.  
- By handling the skip on the client side, PipePipe sidesteps the need for any server‑side ad‑tech, preserving bandwidth and reducing latency.  
- It also raises an interesting governance question: as the blocklist grows, who decides what counts as a “sponsor” and how do we keep the filter transparent?

I’m curious—do you think native SponsorBlock support will make open‑source YouTube clients a viable daily alternative for most users, or will platform restrictions eventually erode that advantage?
